sections.model_projection: The model projects Tulane to win at home 32-21, a margin of 11.6 points, with a projected total of 52.8. Tulane's win probability sits at 77.7%. The market has Tulane favored by 9.5 points with a total of 49.5, meaning the model sees the Green Wave as roughly 2 points stronger than the line and the total about 3 points higher than the market number.
sections.offensive_matchup: Tulane's offense holds a meaningful edge in the passing game, posting an opponent-adjusted passing EPA per play (expected points added per pass attempt, measuring efficiency above average) of 0.36 versus South Alabama's pass defense, which ranks 121st nationally at 0.43 EPA allowed per pass play. That combination creates a significant mismatch: Tulane's quarterbacks should find room to operate against a Jaguar secondary that has been one of the most exploitable in the country so far. South Alabama's offense is run-heavy — their neutral-script pass rate of 42% ranks 118th — and while their rushing EPA per play (0.10) is modestly positive, they face a Tulane run defense that is roughly average, so the ground game alone is unlikely to generate enough volume to keep pace. South Alabama's overall offensive success rate of 38% ranks 116th, meaning they are failing to gain the required yardage on a high share of plays, which will make sustained drives difficult.
sections.quarterback_edge: South Alabama's Bishop Davenport carries a slight edge in the model's quarterback index, built on 411 career attempts at 65.9% completion and 6.58 yards per attempt across 15 games with significant action. Tulane's Kadin Semonza has more career volume — 530 attempts, 63.4% completion, 6.64 yards per attempt over 17 games — but is flagged as having no prior data in the current system context, and his career EPA per dropback is unavailable for both passers, limiting the depth of this comparison. The edge is narrow and leans slightly toward Davenport, but neither quarterback separates himself meaningfully on the available career box-score metrics.
sections.trenches: Tulane's offensive line holds a clear advantage in pass protection: their sack rate allowed of 3.5% ranks 29th nationally, while South Alabama's pass-rush sack rate of 3.5% ranks 128th — the Jaguars generate very little pressure. That mismatch gives Semonza a clean pocket and supports Tulane's passing attack. In the run game, South Alabama's offensive line yards per rush (3.0, rank 65th) are middling, and Tulane's defensive line yards allowed (2.95, rank 88th) are also average, making the ground-game trench battle roughly a wash. The defensive front edge favors South Alabama slightly in the model, as the Jaguars' run defense has been stout in opponent-adjusted metrics (rank 60th in rushing EPA allowed), but Tulane's protection advantage is the more impactful trench factor in this matchup.
sections.explosive_play_edge: Tulane holds a modest edge in the explosive-play category. South Alabama's defense has allowed explosive plays (10-plus rushing, 20-plus passing yards) on 14.1% of opponent snaps, ranking 117th nationally, while Tulane's offense generates explosives on 10.8% of plays. Conversely, South Alabama's offense has produced explosives on only 9.6% of plays — ranking 122nd — against a Tulane defense that has allowed them on 12.7% of snaps. The net result is that Tulane is better positioned to hit the big play, and South Alabama's defense is the more vulnerable unit in this dimension.
sections.third_down_red_zone: South Alabama owns a significant third-down edge: their conversion rate of 42.6% ranks 53rd offensively, and their defense has held opponents to just 28.7% on third down, ranking 9th nationally. Tulane converts only 37.1% of third downs offensively (rank 100th) and allows 41.2% defensively (rank 100th), so the Jaguars should win the third-down battle if they can get into manageable situations. However, the red-zone picture flips sharply: South Alabama's defense has allowed touchdowns on 73.4% of opponent red-zone trips (rank 111th), while Tulane's offense converts at only 44.6% (rank 135th, flagged low sample). South Alabama's offense scores touchdowns on 77.2% of their own red-zone trips (rank 28th), but Tulane's defense has allowed TDs on only 58.4% of trips (rank 51st), so the red-zone battle is mixed and both teams' small-sample red-zone numbers should be treated with caution.
sections.roster_talent: Tulane holds a meaningful talent advantage: their roster talent percentile sits at 49th nationally with a four-year blue-chip ratio of 4%, compared to South Alabama's 29th percentile and 0% blue-chip ratio. South Alabama, however, brings far superior roster continuity — a continuity index of 0.70 versus Tulane's 0.14 — meaning the Jaguars return significantly more of their production from prior seasons. Tulane underwent a head-coach change and returns just 24% of total production (0% of passing production), making this one of the most rebuilt rosters in the country. South Alabama returns 49% of total production with a stable coaching staff, which partially offsets the raw talent gap.
sections.recent_form: Both teams have played exactly one game, so recent form is based on a single-game sample with no multi-game trend to evaluate. South Alabama scored 39 points and allowed 14 in their opener, while Tulane scored just 3 points and allowed 17. The opponent-adjusted blend metrics moderate both results significantly — South Alabama's strength of schedule ranks 89th while Tulane's ranks 137th — meaning Tulane's weak offensive showing came against a weaker opponent and South Alabama's strong showing came against a tougher one. The model's recent-form shift is zero for both teams, reflecting the absence of a meaningful trend from one game.

sections.expected_game_script: Tulane should control the game's tempo from the home sideline, operating at a measured pace (28.3 seconds per play, rank 74th) while leaning on a passing attack that has a genuine efficiency edge against South Alabama's vulnerable secondary. South Alabama will counter by running the ball frequently — their pass rate of 39% ranks 125th — and trying to grind clock with a fast-paced, run-first approach that generates high play volume. The Jaguars' third-down defense (rank 9th) gives them a real chance to force Tulane into punting situations, keeping the game from becoming a blowout early. However, South Alabama's own offense will struggle to sustain drives against a Tulane defense that, on an opponent-adjusted basis, has been solid overall (rank 48th in defensive EPA per play), and the Jaguars' 38% offensive success rate suggests frequent three-and-outs. If Tulane can convert red-zone trips — their biggest offensive weakness — into touchdowns rather than field goals, the margin grows; if they stall inside the 20, South Alabama's turnover margin edge (rank 33rd) and third-down conversion ability (43%) keep them competitive. The model sees a double-digit Tulane win, but Tulane's roster uncertainty and South Alabama's continuity advantage make a closer game plausible.
